rationale: C10 plausibly supplied a material contractor-claim template: it rejects extra payment beyond a written government contract, emphasizes that the contract imposed no further governmental obligation, warns against a precedent benefiting contractors despite their contractual terms, and invokes unfair preferential treatment relative to other government contractors. The child compresses this same machinery into a short veto memorandum concerning services performed beyond a written contract. C07 shares the narrower warning that compensating services outside formal employment or contracting arrangements would encourage similar claims, while C17 parallels the refusal to relieve one contractor from contractual losses at the expense of other contractors; neither aligns as fully as C10.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This payment would be for services rendered by the beneficiary in excess of its written contract with the Government.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It contained no provision for payment of additional compensation merely because the contractor might suffer a loss in performance... there is no liability for any further payment to the contractor, based upon the contract provisions.
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the private bill as an attempt to impose additional government payment beyond the obligations fixed by a written contract.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Approval of this legislation could well encourage others to perform unauthorized work and expect payment therefor from the Government.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: My approval of this bill would establish the undesirable principle of Government underwriting any wartime losses incurred by contractors providing goods and services to the Government
shared_material.explanation: Both reject approval because it would establish an adverse payment principle extending beyond the individual claimant.

shared_material.child_excerpt: this organization would receive preferential treatment which has in the past been denied other research contractors who performed work in excess of their contract obligations.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am unable to perceive any circumstances which would warrant preferential treatment for the claimant to the detriment of other wartime contractors.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts C10's comparative preferential-treatment rationale to a different class of government contractors.
